summary: Dive mini-game drop-effect timing object: holds a pointer to its owning Dive window/actor object, an embedded slot-sequence object used as start gate, a 60-frame start delay counter and a threshold float copied here from a per-monster lookup row; methods sit in the Dive method table next to Dive_SpawnDropEffect (0x7254B8).
evidence: Dive_Effect_InitFromActor (0x0032A75C) reads owner->u16@0x238, looks it up through the lazily built table passed to 0x0063E5C8 and stores row->u16@0xE2 * constant into self->f_A0; Dive_Effect_UpdateStartDelay (0x0032B0C8) gates on f_38==0x3C and then requests state 2 on the embedded object at +0x2C; both functions were recovered by R3_065 with conf 0.50 and sit in the 0x7254B8 method table next to Dive_SpawnDropEffect (0x0032AC88) and the sibling cluster Ui_DiveEffect (0x0032A850) which shares the +0x28/+0x2C/+0xA0 field shape. No allocation site seen for size 164 (max_strong_field+width), so the exact size/layout is only weakly supported.

fields.name: unknown_sharedTableArtifact
fields.evidence: Spurious: the 'write' struct_db attributed to offset 0 ('*puVar4 = uRam0032a848;' in 0x0032A75C) stores through the freshly allocated shared-table pointer (puVar4 = alloc via 0x0011CFDC, afterwards *globalCache = puVar4), never through param_1/self - param_1 is not written anywhere in the body. The first word belongs to the shared lookup table consumed by 0x0063E5C8, not to DiveEffect; treated as an alias artifact rather than a real member.

fields.name: maybe_ownerObject
fields.evidence: Read once in 0x0032A75C: sVar1 = *(u16*)(*(int*)(self+0x28) + 0x238), used as the monster/visual id for the table lookup (sibling callers of the same family show more of this object: maybe_Ui_DiveEffect_Update calls owner->vt[+0x98] and reads owner u16@0x242 / u8@0x244 / u32@0x248 / u8@0x24C; Dive_SpawnDropEffect reads owner floats +0x9C..+0xA4 as XYZ position and +0x248 as a Gfx handle). So +0x28 is a pointer to the owning Dive window/actor object; its exact class (Ui_DiveWindow-family vs Field actor) is not proven here, hence maybe_.

fields.name: maybe_slotSequenceObj
fields.evidence: Embedded polymorphic sub-object at +0x2C: 0x0032B0C8 calls sub->vt[+0x14](sub, 2) and, if it returns nonzero, sub->vt[+0x10](sub) - a state-request with id 2 followed by commit. The adjacent same-family cluster Ui_DiveEffect uses the same +0x2C area as its effect-slot sequence (states 1/2 at self+0x40.., count at +0x48), and Ui_DiveForm (0x0032A75C relative cluster) shows the identical idiom '(**(code**)(*(int*)(x+0x11c)+0x14))(x+0x11c, 0x17)'. What abstract type the vtable belongs to is not provable from these two fragments, so a descriptive maybe_ name.

fields.name: startDelayFrameCount
fields.evidence: Dive_Effect_UpdateStartDelay (0x0032B0C8) tests exactly 'self->f_38 == 0x3C' (60) and on equality runs the request/commit pair, i.e. the effect's actions start once this counter reaches 60; the increment lives in a function not recovered in this batch, so only the compare (and hence 'frame delay to start') is sure.

fields.name: maybe_durationThreshold
fields.evidence: Dive_Effect_InitFromActor writes *(float*)(self+0xA0) = VectorUnsignedToFloat(owner_id-row->u16@0xE2) * pooled constant (0x0032A75C), so it is a per-monster derived value; the sibling Ui_DiveEffect_Update (0x0032A850) uses the same-offset f_A0 as the threshold its per-frame f_34 progress is compared against (f_34 < f_A0, then f_34 < f_A0 + constant), which supports 'timing/threshold for the effect' without pinning the unit.
